sources.fact: Historic England lists The Old Granary, Town Quay, Barking as Grade II, list entry 1064418.
The Old Granary was first listed on 17 December 1968.
The statutory address is The Old Granary, Town Quay in Barking and Dagenham.
Historic England describes a mid-19th-century yellow-brick, slate-roofed four-storey granary with tower.
Historic England's archive page states the Old Granary at Town Quay was built in 1870 and is all that remains of Barking Mill.
Planning Data's current listed-building entity for Barking Old Granary reproduces Grade II status and point 0.073711,51.534244 from Historic England.
The listed-building point is not treated as an HMLR title polygon or housing-allocation boundary.
Companies House records a 26 April 2021 registered-office change to Flat 4 Town Quay, The Old Granary, Barking IG11 7AZ.
That company was dissolved on 16 November 2021, so the historic address record is not current ownership or occupancy proof.
Companies House also contains a historical Flat 3, The Old Granary correspondence address, supporting multi-unit address identity only.
Local Plan context is kept separate from listed-building status and from exact current planning-case evidence.
No exact current residential application/decision was verified this wave; current case readback remains required.
